content.text: {"what_it_is":{"claims":[{"text":"Spares and Repair Parts is a Navy program (organization \"N\") that buys the spare and repair parts needed to keep naval and Marine Corps aircraft flying. It is funded under the Aircraft Procurement, Navy account.","citation":{"fact_id":"a767c63490cbe337"}},{"text":"The program is known internally as APN-6, a \"follower\" account that procures all applicable spare and repair parts for Navy and Marine Corps end-items and modifications bought under other Aircraft Procurement, Navy budget activities — meaning its needs track program changes in aircraft quantities, basing plans, installation schedules, and maintenance data.","citation":{"fact_id":"6b0582686403b079"}},{"text":"Spares fall into several categories: Initial spares (parts and spare engines to support newly procured aircraft), spares for modifications, spares for support equipment and training devices, Wholesale Supply Inventory (long-term stock for programs after their Material Support Date), and Replenishment spares (headquarters and fleet outfitting parts).","citation":{"fact_id":"6b0582686403b079"}},{"text":"A large part of the program funds the Aviation Outfitting Account, which stocks carriers and amphibious ships with spare parts to provide 90-day sustainment levels for fielded aircraft such as the F/A-18, H-1, E-2, V-22, P-8, H-60, and MQ-4 while deployed.","citation":{"fact_id":"6b0582686403b079"}}]},"why_it_matters":{"claims":[{"text":"The Navy describes aviation sparing as a strategic investment in readiness, aimed at sustaining both today's deployed forces and the future \"Airwing of the Future,\" and at achieving the Chief of Naval Operations' required 90-day endurance level of repair parts aboard aircraft carriers.","citation":{"fact_id":"e6de031d9fbcd50a"}},{"text":"Stocking more spares aboard deployed carriers is meant to increase mission-capable rates and extend a carrier's time on station without resupply — reducing the logistics burden in a contested environment. Because suppliers have multi-year lead times, the Navy argues spares must be bought today to be ready for future conflict.","citation":{"fact_id":"e6de031d9fbcd50a"}},{"text":"Initial contractor spares, engine spares, and Peculiar Support Equipment are cited as major cost drivers as new aircraft types are introduced, procured, and modified.","citation":{"fact_id":"e6de031d9fbcd50a"}},{"text":"For fiscal year 2026 the F-35C carrier-variant initial spares funding rises from $124.685 million to $160.029 million, driven partly by the Navy and Marine Corps increasing their Afloat Spares Package requirements for the joint aircraft's Global Spares Pool.","citation":{"fact_id":"e6de031d9fbcd50a"}},{"text":"The MQ-25 unmanned tanker sees its first substantial initial-spares buy — up from $0 in FY2025 to $35.797 million in FY2026 — timed to the aircraft's first carrier and shore standups and deployment schedule.","citation":{"fact_id":"e6de031d9fbcd50a"}},{"text":"A newly established Wholesale Supply Inventory cost type appears in FY2026 with $81.412 million, addressing shortfalls in long-term stock and parts obsolescence across numerous platforms.","citation":{"fact_id":"e6de031d9fbcd50a"}},{"text":"The largest single line, Aviation Outfitting Account Repairables, grows from $1,059.646 million to $1,231.978 million in FY2026 to support fleet readiness and a \"Targeted AVCAL Wholeness\" initiative that plans for a 42-day resupply time rather than the previously estimated 10 days.","citation":{"fact_id":"e6de031d9fbcd50a"}},{"text":"The FY2026 request was reduced by $1.836 million for Advisory and Assistance Services and by $0.263 million for civilian personnel, in alignment with executive orders implementing the administration's Department of Government Efficiency initiatives.","citation":{"fact_id":"e6de031d9fbcd50a"}}]},"players":{"claims":[{"text":"Lobbying filings referenced this program: FedEx Corporation reported lobbying activity in a 2026 filing that mentioned repair and parts legislation, including the REPAIR Act.","citation":{"fact_id":"019440805ba04bc0"}},{"text":"A second 2026 FedEx Corporation filing also referenced repair and parts matters. (Lobbying mentions show only that a filing referenced program-related terms, not that any spending decision resulted.)","citation":{"fact_id":"011d6ee62d525049"}}]},"recent_developments":{"claims":[]}}
